decisions.quote: By generating bovine and porcine DNAJC14 knockout cells, we could show that (i) replication of 6 distinct noncp pestivirus species (A to D, F, and G) depends on DNAJC14, (ii) the pestiviral replicase NS3-5B can assemble into functional complexes in the absence of DNAJC14, and (iii) all cp pestiviruses replicate their RNA and generate infectious progeny independent of host DNAJC14. Together, these findings confirm DNAJC14 as a pivotal cellular cofactor for the replication and maintenance of the noncp biotype of pestiviruses.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and the blind coder classify this study as a replication. Using newly generated CRISPR/Cas9 DNAJC14-knockout and GST-Jiv90 rescue cell lines, the authors collect new experimental data that directly re-test and confirm the previously published finding that BVDV-1 (and other noncp pestiviruses) depend on cellular DNAJC14/Jiv90 for regulated NS2-3 cleavage and RNA replication.

This study is a replication that generates new CRISPR/Cas9 DNAJC14-knockout and GST-Jiv90 rescue cell lines to re-test and extend previously published findings on DNAJC14 dependency. Both the shipped record and blind target 1 identify Reference 15 (Lackner et al., 2005, doi: 10.1128/jvi.79.15.9746-9755.2005) as the replicated original study, which established that cellular DNAJC14 (Jiv/Jiv90) determines BVDV-1 NS2-3 cleavage regulation, noncp RNA replication, and persistence, and supplied the GST-Jiv90(WT) and GST-Jiv90(W39A) constructs re-tested in Fig. 5 and Fig. 6. In contrast, the other two references flagged by the blind coder are not separate replication targets: Reference 14 (Lackner et al., 2004, target 0) is an earlier study in the same chain cited as background for baseline NCP7 vs. CP7 replication differences in naive MDBK control cells, and Reference 53 (Lackner et al., 2006, target 2) is cited in the Introduction and Discussion for mechanistic interpretation of the Reference 15 GST-Jiv90 rescue experiment regarding NS2 binding domains and J-domain independence.

decisions.quote: The functional importance of DNAJC14 for noncp pestiviruses has been established so far only for BVDV-1. It was therefore enigmatic whether replication of other noncp pestiviruses is also DNAJC14 dependent. By generating bovine and porcine DNAJC14 knockout cells, we could show that (i) replication of 6 distinct noncp pestivirus species (A to D, F, and G) depends on DNAJC14, (ii) the pestiviral replicase NS3-5B can assemble into functional complexes in the absence of DNAJC14, and (iii) all cp pestiviruses replicate their RNA and generate infectious progeny independent of host DNAJC14. Together, these findings confirm DNAJC14 as a pivotal cellular cofactor for the replication and maintenance of the noncp biotype of pestiviruses.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind target 1 code the replication outcome for Lackner et al. (2005) (Reference 15) as successful. Using newly generated CRISPR/Cas9 DNAJC14-knockout and GST-Jiv90(WT)/GST-Jiv90(W39A) rescue cell lines, the authors confirm both overall and in direct experimental comparisons to Reference 15 that noncp BVDV-1 (and five additional pestivirus species) require functional DNAJC14/Jiv90 for regulated NS2-3 cleavage and viral RNA replication, whereas cp pestiviruses replicate independently of endogenous DNAJC14, and that GST-Jiv90(WT) rescue restores NCP7 replication and deregulates NS2-3 cleavage without complete cleavage, in agreement with Reference 15.
